findings.description: The full-tree release commit can include credentials in tracked or non-ignored files.
findings.analysis: The release contract deliberately stages all non-ignored working-tree content. The project's security policy prohibits committing secrets, but the release skill does not itself run a dedicated secret scanner before staging.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether the existing repository secret controls are sufficient or release preparation should run an explicit configured secret check before commit.
findings.rationale: The repository already prohibits committing secrets and uses its established controls. A release-only scanner adds unnecessary process.

findings.description: A GitHub query failure is not explicitly described as a release blocker.
findings.analysis: The skill requires querying GitHub before branch creation but does not state what to do when that query cannot establish the open-PR state.
findings.recommendation: Make a failed or incomplete GitHub query stop release preparation.
findings.rationale: A failed GitHub query is surfaced as an operational error. The workflow does not need an additional defensive branch for a hypothetical incomplete result.

findings.description: A stale local delivery branch can omit already delivered upstream commits.
findings.analysis: The skill creates the release branch from the configured delivery branch but does not explicitly synchronise or compare it with its upstream first.
findings.recommendation: Fetch and ensure the delivery branch is current before branching for the release.
findings.rationale: A release branch must start from the current delivery branch so it contains every delivered commit.

findings.description: Manifest generation executes the local package before the full candidate is shown.
findings.analysis: The command intentionally runs the repository's current package to produce its manifest. Treating this as an untrusted-execution boundary conflicts with the developer-directed release workflow.
findings.recommendation: Retain the local manifest command unless the project establishes a separate trusted release tool.
findings.rationale: `uv run specle manifest` is the intended project-scoped command resolution. A separate trusted release tool is not required.

findings.description: PEP 440 epoch versions are accepted by comparison but rejected by the manifest format.
findings.analysis: The manifest version grammar excludes `!`, so an epoch can pass the stated PEP 440 comparison and fail only after release preparation has begun.
findings.recommendation: Validate the proposed version against both PEP 440 and the manifest format during preflight.
findings.rationale: The release version must be valid for both package metadata and the manifest before release preparation changes files.

findings.description: A valid non-canonical PEP 440 spelling can differ from the normalized reported package version.
findings.analysis: The skill compares the manifest command's raw reported value with the raw proposal, so normalization may appear as a false mismatch after files have changed.
findings.recommendation: Normalize the accepted proposed version before writing and comparing it.
findings.rationale: Derive one canonical PEP 440 form and use it consistently for pyproject.toml, branch naming, manifest generation, manifest verification, and the commit title.

findings.description: A selected change or open PR can appear after preflight but before the release commit.
findings.analysis: This is a concurrency scenario between preflight and commit. The repository is presently single-user and does not establish concurrent release preparation as a supported workflow.
findings.recommendation: Retain the single preflight unless concurrent release actors become an established delivery model.
findings.rationale: The repository's current single-user delivery model does not support or require concurrent release preparation.

findings.description: Version comparison can use a different branch's pyproject version than the branch later used for release.
findings.analysis: The skill's order reads the current checkout before switching to the delivery branch, so a non-main checkout could supply a stale or lower comparison baseline.
findings.recommendation: Read the version from the configured delivery branch before accepting the release version.
findings.rationale: The checked-out pyproject.toml is the sole authority for release versions. Release preparation does not infer a competing value from another branch.

findings.description: The deliberately broad release commit does not require project checks or local review immediately before committing.
findings.analysis: The skill presents and commits every working-tree change, but it does not establish which verification evidence applies to that assembled candidate.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether release preparation should require a fresh project quality-gate run for the final candidate.
findings.rationale: The release workflow's explicit full-candidate review and user authorisation are the intended control. It does not require a second local-review lifecycle for the assembled release commit.

findings.description: Concurrent manifest generation can lose another release's appended records.
findings.analysis: This assumes concurrent release runs writing one manifest. The repository does not establish concurrent release preparation as supported.
findings.recommendation: Retain the current manifest operation unless concurrent releases become a supported model.
findings.rationale: Concurrent release preparation is outside the repository's delivery model.

findings.description: A manifest version mismatch can append a record before release preparation stops.
findings.analysis: The current order runs the append-only command before checking its reported version, so a mismatch leaves a durable manifest entry even though no release commit is made.
findings.recommendation: Validate the accepted normalized version before invocation, or otherwise ensure a mismatch cannot append a manifest generation.
findings.rationale: Preflight canonicalisation and manifest-format validation are sufficient. The manifest command remains the authoritative append-only operation.

findings.description: A selected but complete change can unnecessarily block release preparation.
findings.analysis: The skill blocks whenever a selector exists, whereas the lifecycle treats externally delivered work as effectively complete pending archival finalisation.
findings.recommendation: Inspect the selected record and block only when its state is not effectively complete.
findings.rationale: Any .specle/current-change selector blocks release preparation. The selector is the deliberate boundary regardless of the selected change's lifecycle status.
